text:
maria: Hey team — we need help with quota increases for a private Dedicated rollout in us-west-2. Spinning up 180 GPU nodes (p4d-ish) and the networking plan requires lots of NLB target groups + interface endpoints. Running into limits when we try to provision.
leo: Ugh. Which quotas are we hitting exactly?
akshay: The deploy failed earlier with two errors from the infra scripts: `ExceededTargetGroupsPerLoadBalancer` and `EndpointLimitExceeded`. Logs attached to the deploy job.
diane: We usually hit the interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) per-VPC limit and the per-load-balancer target group cap. Default counts are low for scale.
maria: Yep. Current cloud account shows: NLB target groups per region = 50, Interface endpoints per VPC = 20, ENIs per instance ~15 — all too small for our design. We also want sticky per-GPU instance target groups for flow-based routing.
leo: Quick ask to AWS: bump NLB target groups per region to 1000, interface endpoints per VPC to 250, and ENIs per instance to 50 for the instance types we plan to use.
akshay: Can we justify numbers? AWS likes concrete numbers + architecture notes. I'll draft the support case.\maria: Draft please. Include expected steady state + headroom: 180 nodes, ~2 target groups per node (can be 1.5 avg), plus spares for blue/green => ~400 target groups. Request 1000 to avoid repeated requests.\diane: Also request increase for TargetGroupTargets (targets per target group) — default sometimes limited by target health registration. And ask for NLB rule limit increases if we need per-target listener rules.\infra-bot: Reminder: quota requests should include account id, region, resource type, current limit, requested limit, and detailed justification per AWS support template. See https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home#/case/create?issueType=service-limit-increase.\maria: Drafted body below (copy/paste into support case):
````
Account ID: 123456789012
Region: us-west-2
Resources and requested limits:
 - NLB target groups (per region): current 50 -> requested 1000
 - Interface VPC endpoints (per VPC): current 20 -> requested 250
 - Elastic Network Interfaces (per instance for p4d): current 15 -> requested 50
 - Targets per target group: current 1000 -> requested 5000 (if applicable)
Justification: Redwood Inference is deploying a Dedicated GPU fleet to support low-latency model inference for customers. We plan to provision 180 GPU instances across private subnets. Our architecture pins individual model shards and routes small fanout traffic through NLB target groups per GPU instance for better locality and health isolation. Each instance will be represented by 1-3 target groups depending on model packing; we need headroom for blue/green rollouts, canary tests, and future expansion. PrivateLink endpoints are used to expose service APIs to customer VPCs and for internal control-plane connectivity; we need more interface endpoints per VPC to attach per-customer endpoints and cross-account services.
Impact of delay: If quota increases are not granted within 5 business days, Dedicated rollout will be blocked, causing customer onboarding delays and potential contract impacts.
Usage pattern: steady-state 180 instances, peak bursts up to 220 for short tests.
````
maria: Anyone want to edit before I open the case?
akshay: Add cost callouts: we accept the hourly cost of endpoints but say we will minimize by consolidating where possible. AWS sometimes asks for cost/reasoning.\diane: Also list the dependent limits: security group rule limits and VPC IP address capacity. We should mention we will use /19s per AZ.\leo: I'll add that we can accept conditional increases (e.g., limit applied only to the listed instance types and the region). Safer for AWS to approve.\maria: Good call. I'll open the ticket and paste the draft. Assigning to akshay for follow-up with AWS support.\aws-bot: Case opened: #CASE-2026-00012345 - Service limit increase request submitted. Estimated response 24-72 hours.\akshay: Got it. I'll monitor and reply if they ask for more detail. If AWS pushes back we should have an alternative: consolidate target groups by using path-based routing or shared proxy instances to reduce targets/groups.\diane: Also think about long-term architecture: if AWS is rigid, we can centralize routing at a fleet of L7 proxies which reduces target group counts but increases latency/cost. Keep that as fallback.\maria: Thanks all. Will update thread with case ID and outcome. :thumbsup:
